Olivia (CSE): Hey team, customer on Private VPC is seeing intermittent TLS handshake failures when streaming inference. Happens ~1/200 requests, started after they pushed a firewall change yesterday. Error from client: "tls: handshake failure". They can repro with curl sometimes.
Emily (Support): Thanks — can you paste the minimal repro and the timeframe? Any recent NAT/egress changes?
Olivia (CSE): Repro steps they gave: `curl -v --http2 https://inference.example.corp/v1/stream -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' --data-binary @prompt.json`  -> 3/10 show `TLS handshake error` in client logs. They said ops only touched security-group and NACL rules.
Marcus (Eng-Oncall): Is this only streaming endpoints or also non-streaming generation? Also which client OS/lib (go/py)?
Olivia (CSE): Mainly streaming but they've also seen sporadic failures on short sync requests. Client is Go 1.20 using crypto/tls. We have logs from the control plane showing successful connection then abrupt TLS alert on backend side for same flow id.
Rajan (NetEng): Can you grab a tcpdump (SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK) and TLS alerts? If NACL is stateless and ephemeral return ports aren't allowed we can see odd mid-handshake resets. Ask them to capture on a worker and on the NAT gateway.
Olivia (CSE): They uploaded a pcap snippet. Key bits: repeated SYN, SYN-ACK, then client sends TLS ClientHello, server responds with Alert(Handshake Failure) and then RST. Also sometimes server never responds.
Emily (Support): Two quick checks while we triage: 1) verify NACL rules allow high ephemeral ports back from inference hosts, 2) check SG egress/ingress ordering for the ALB/NAT. Can you paste `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --network-acl-ids <id>` and the security group rules?
Olivia (CSE): Paste from customer (sanitized): NACL has allow 443 inbound, allow 443 outbound, and explicit DENY for ports 32768-65535 outbound. SG allows 443 outbound from worker to inference-hosts. Ops says they thought only 443 needed to be open.
Marcus (Eng-Oncall): That's the problem. TLS requires ephemeral client ports for return TCP — stateless NACL DENY on ephemeral range will drop the dynamic return path. For streaming we keep connections alive and reuse sockets so occasional allocation can hit denied ports. Recommend removing the explicit DENY and instead whitelist required ranges.
Rajan (NetEng): Also check NAT port allocation: some NAT devices use ports in the 1024-65535 space; if NACL denies 32768-65535 you'll still see many failures. Best practice: allow ephemeral 1024-65535 outbound (or at least 32768-61000 depending on OS).
Olivia (CSE): Customer asked for exact change. What's minimal safe change?
Marcus (Eng-Oncall): Minimal: in the NACL outbound rules, allow TCP ports 1024-65535 to destination 0.0.0.0/0 (or at least the inference subnet CIDR). If policy prohibits that, allow ephemeral range used by their NAT (check `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range`).
Emily (Support): If they can't change NACL quickly, a short mitigation is to route inference egress through a managed NAT that you can control, or use our Hosted fallback for streams for affected customers. But that's a workaround.
Rajan (NetEng): Also confirm there are no middleboxes doing TLS inspection that might rewrite ALPN/SNI causing `handshake failure`. The pcap shows server Alert, which usually means server aborted negotiation (cipher/ALPN mismatch) — but given timing and DENY rule, I lean NACL.
Olivia (CSE): I asked them to run `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range` and check NAT logs. They responded: `32768 60999`. So ephemeral range overlaps denied range.
Marcus (Eng-Oncall): Bingo. Ask them to temporarily remove the DENY for 32768-65535 outbound and retest. Also capture tcpdump after change to confirm stable 3-way and TLS handshake completes.
Olivia (CSE): Sent instructions and a test curl command to validate: `curl -v --http2 --resolve inference.example.corp:443:<inference-host-ip> https://inference.example.corp/v1/stream -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'`.
infra-bot: Deployment notice: we rolled a small control-plane patch 2h ago but it only touched metrics; not related to TLS.
Emily (Support): Thanks infra-bot. Olivia, once customer confirms fix, request they share success sample (client logs + one pcap) so we can close. Also capture server-side accept logs to correlate.
Olivia (CSE): Customer removed the DENY and confirmed streaming success in 30/30 requests. They sent client log: `TLS handshake complete, negotiated TLS1.3, ALPN h2`.
Marcus (Eng-Oncall): Great. Action items: Rajan to add a KB note about VPC NACLs vs ephemeral ports for inference streaming; Emily to follow up with customer for postmortem and closing ticket.
Rajan (NetEng): I'll draft the KB: include `ip_local_port_range`, recommended ranges to allow (1024-65535), example AWS NACL rules, and a note about NAT port allocation.
Emily (Support): Marking this thread resolved pending KB and postmortem. :white_check_mark:
Olivia (CSE): Customer appreciative. Leaving their contact for follow-up.
Marcus (Eng-Oncall): Adding one more: if customers use strict NACL rules, recommend stateful SGs + managed NAT rather than stateless NACL DENY on ephemeral ranges — saves a lot of subtle socket issues.
Olivia (CSE): Thanks all, closing here after KB published.
